entries.meaning: Add has 3 distinct senses.
examples: "And bring your passport," she added.
Would you like to add anything before we finish?
He has added a note at the bottom of the letter.
If you add 15 and 27, you get 42.
She added the three columns twice to be sure.
He checked the bill, adding the figures in his head.
Add a little salt to the sauce.
They added a second bathroom last year.
We are adding two more chairs to the table.

senses.head: To say something more after what has already been said
examples: "And bring your passport," she added.
Would you like to add anything before we finish?
He has added a note at the bottom of the letter.

senses.head: To put two or more numbers together to get a total
examples: If you add 15 and 27, you get 42.
She added the three columns twice to be sure.
He checked the bill, adding the figures in his head.

senses.head: To put something with something else to make it bigger, better, or complete
examples: Add a little salt to the sauce.
They added a second bathroom last year.
We are adding two more chairs to the table.

entries.русский: добавлять, добавить (сказать ещё); складывать, сложить (числа); прибавлять, прибавить; добавлять, добавить; прибавлять
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (add a comment), intransitive ("That's all," he added)
entries.phrasal verbs: add in · add on · add to · add up · add up · add up · add up to

entries.meaning: Address has 3 distinct senses.
examples: The mayor will address the city council tonight.
She addressed the crowd from the steps of the library.
He was addressing the students when the fire alarm went off.
The mayor promised to address the housing shortage.
Your letter addressed none of my questions.
The report has addressed every complaint on the list.
Address the envelope to the head office.
The package was addressed to my old apartment.
She spent the morning addressing holiday cards.

senses.head: To speak formally to a person or a group
examples: The mayor will address the city council tonight.
She addressed the crowd from the steps of the library.
He was addressing the students when the fire alarm went off.

senses.head: To give attention to a problem and try to deal with it
examples: The mayor promised to address the housing shortage.
Your letter addressed none of my questions.
The report has addressed every complaint on the list.

senses.head: To write on a letter or package the name and place it is being sent to
examples: Address the envelope to the head office.
The package was addressed to my old apartment.
She spent the morning addressing holiday cards.

entries.русский: обращаться, обратиться (к кому-л.); выступать перед; заниматься (проблемой), решать; рассматривать (вопрос); адресовать, надписывать адрес
entries.contrast: The verb is always uh-DRES; the noun (where you live) is usually AD-res in American English.

entries.meaning: Admit has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I admit I was wrong about the date.
She finally admitted that she had forgotten his birthday.
He has never admitted his part in it.
This ticket admits two people.
The college admitted only a tenth of its applicants.
She was admitted to the hospital overnight.

senses.head: To agree, often unwillingly, that something bad or embarrassing is true
examples: I admit I was wrong about the date.
She finally admitted that she had forgotten his birthday.
He has never admitted his part in it.

senses.head: To allow someone to enter a place, a school, or a hospital
body: (впускать, впустить; принимать, принять (в больницу, в вуз))
examples: This ticket admits two people.
The college admitted only a tenth of its applicants.
She was admitted to the hospital overnight.

entries.русский: признавать, признать; сознаваться, сознаться; впускать, впустить; принимать, принять (в больницу, в вуз)
entries.contrast: The single t doubles before an ending: admit → admitted → admitting.

entries.meaning: Advise has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The doctor advised him to rest for a week.
I'd advise you to read the contract twice.
She has been advising the company since January.
Please advise us of any change of address.
We were advised that the flight had been canceled.
The clerk is advising passengers of the delay.

senses.head: To tell someone what you think they should do
examples: The doctor advised him to rest for a week.
I'd advise you to read the contract twice.
She has been advising the company since January.

senses.head: To tell someone a piece of information formally or officially
examples: Please advise us of any change of address.
We were advised that the flight had been canceled.
The clerk is advising passengers of the delay.

entries.русский: советовать, посоветовать; уведомлять, уведомить; извещать, сообщать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (advise students), intransitive (I would advise against it)
entries.contrast: advise is the verb and ends in a /z/ sound; advice is the noun and ends in /s/: "She advised me, so I took her advice."

entries.meaning: To have the same opinion as someone else, or to say yes to a plan. ---
examples: I agree with almost everything in her report.
They agreed to meet at the corner at noon.
We have never agreed about politics.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (I agree that it's late), intransitive (we all agree)
entries.contrast: Keep both e's and add nothing extra: agree → agreed → agreeing, never "agreeed" or "agred".
entries.phrasal verbs: agree with, agree to, agree on

entries.meaning: To tell people about something officially or publicly. ---
examples: The airline will announce the new schedule on Friday.
They announced their engagement at dinner.
The winners have already been announced.

entries.meaning: To say you are sorry for something you have done. ---
examples: You should apologize to your sister.
He apologized for being late.
She left without apologizing.
entries.contrast: American spelling is apologize; British books write apologise. You apologize to a person for a thing.

entries.meaning: To disagree with someone in words, or to give reasons for an opinion. ---
examples: My neighbors argue about money every weekend.
She argued that the test was unfair.
They have been arguing since breakfast.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (he argued that the law was unfair), intransitive (they argue constantly)
entries.contrast: The silent e drops before -ing: argue → arguing, not "argueing".
entries.phrasal verbs: argue with, argue about, argue over

entries.meaning: Ask has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Can I ask you something?
She asked me where the bathroom was.
Nobody has asked about the money yet.
How much are they asking for the house on the corner?
He asked too much for the old truck, so nobody bought it.
Don't ask more than the car is actually worth.
They asked nearly a hundred people to the wedding.
We're asking the neighbors to dinner on Saturday.
I haven't asked him to the party yet.

senses.head: To say something to someone in order to get an answer or a favor
examples: Can I ask you something?
She asked me where the bathroom was.
Nobody has asked about the money yet.

senses.head: To want a particular price for something you are selling
examples: How much are they asking for the house on the corner?
He asked too much for the old truck, so nobody bought it.
Don't ask more than the car is actually worth.

senses.head: To invite someone to an event or to your home
examples: They asked nearly a hundred people to the wedding.
We're asking the neighbors to dinner on Saturday.
I haven't asked him to the party yet.

entries.русский: спрашивать, спросить; просить, попросить; просить (цену), запрашивать; приглашать, пригласить (в гости, на праздник)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (ask a question), intransitive (if you don't know, ask)
entries.contrast: In American English say /æsk/, not /ɑːsk/ — and ask me, never "ask to me".
entries.phrasal verbs: ask after · ask around · ask for · ask for · ask for, ask about · ask out · ask over

entries.meaning: To tell someone confidently that something is true so that they stop worrying. ---
examples: I can assure you the package is on its way.
The nurse assured him that the pain would pass.
We have been assured that the water is safe.
entries.contrast: assure a person, ensure a result, insure a car: "I assure you the car is insured."

entries.meaning: To ask for something in a very urgent, humble way. ---
examples: Don't make me beg.
He begged her not to tell anyone.
The dog sat begging under the table.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (she begged him to stay), intransitive (a man was begging on the corner)
entries.contrast: Double the g: beg → begged → begging.

entries.meaning: To say that someone or something is responsible for something bad. ---
examples: Don't blame the weather for your bad mood.
They blamed the driver for the accident.
I have never blamed you for what happened.
entries.contrast: You blame a person for a thing, or blame a thing on a person.

entries.meaning: To talk with too much pride about what you have or what you have done. ---
examples: He likes to brag about his car.
She bragged that she had finished in an hour.
They kept bragging all through dinner.
entries.contrast: Double the g: brag → bragged → bragging.

entries.meaning: Call has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Call me when you land.
I called the office twice this morning.
Somebody has been calling and hanging up.
They called the baby Maya.
What do you call this in English?
The street was once called Mill Road.
The governor called a special session.
The union has called a strike for Monday.
The coach calls a timeout with a minute left.

senses.head: To telephone someone, or to say someone's name loudly to get their attention
examples: Call me when you land.
I called the office twice this morning.
Somebody has been calling and hanging up.

senses.head: To give someone or something a name, or to use a particular name for them
examples: They called the baby Maya.
What do you call this in English?
The street was once called Mill Road.

senses.head: To order something official to take place and summon people to it
examples: The governor called a special session.
The union has called a strike for Monday.
The coach calls a timeout with a minute left.

entries.русский: звонить, позвонить; звать, позвать; называть, назвать; называть, назвать; звать (по имени); созывать, созвать; объявлять, объявить (забастовку, собрание)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (call your mother), intransitive (she called from the airport)
entries.phrasal verbs: call around · call back · call for · call forth · call in · call in · call off · call on · call out · call up · call up

entries.meaning: To talk in a friendly, informal way. ---
examples: We can chat after the meeting.
They chatted in the parking lot for an hour.
She was chatting with a neighbor when I drove up.
entries.contrast: Double the t: chat → chatted → chatting.

entries.meaning: Chatter has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The kids chatter the whole way to school.
She chattered nervously while we waited.
I could hear them chattering in the next room.
His teeth were chattering by the time we got inside.
My teeth chattered all the way home.
Her teeth chatter whenever she climbs out of the pool.

senses.head: To talk quickly and continuously about unimportant things
examples: The kids chatter the whole way to school.
She chattered nervously while we waited.
I could hear them chattering in the next room.

senses.head: (of teeth) To knock together quickly because of cold or fear
examples: His teeth were chattering by the time we got inside.
My teeth chattered all the way home.
Her teeth chatter whenever she climbs out of the pool.

entries.русский: болтать, тараторить; стучать (о зубах), клацать зубами

entries.meaning: To shout loudly to show support or approval. ---
examples: The whole stadium began to cheer.
They cheered when the power came back on.
A crowd was cheering outside the courthouse.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (the fans cheered the team), intransitive (everyone cheered)

entries.meaning: Claim has 3 distinct senses.
examples: He claims he never got the email.
She claimed to be a doctor.
Two groups have claimed responsibility.
You can claim a refund within thirty days.
She claimed the prize the next morning.
Nobody has claimed the wallet that was turned in.
House fires claim hundreds of lives every winter.
The storm claimed four lives in one county.
The crash has claimed a fifth victim.

senses.head: To say that something is true even though it has not been proved
examples: He claims he never got the email.
She claimed to be a doctor.
Two groups have claimed responsibility.

senses.head: To officially ask for money or property that you have a right to
examples: You can claim a refund within thirty days.
She claimed the prize the next morning.
Nobody has claimed the wallet that was turned in.

senses.head: Of an accident or a disaster, to take someone's life
examples: House fires claim hundreds of lives every winter.
The storm claimed four lives in one county.
The crash has claimed a fifth victim.

entries.русский: утверждать; заявлять, заявить; требовать, востребовать; получать по праву, оформлять (возврат); уносить, унести (жизни)

entries.meaning: To make something easier to understand by explaining it more fully. ---
examples: Could you clarify what you mean by "soon"?
The teacher clarified the instructions.
Nothing has been clarified yet.
entries.contrast: The y becomes ie: clarify → clarifies → clarified.

entries.meaning: To say or write something that gives an opinion about someone or something. ---
examples: The senator refused to comment.
Several readers commented on the photo.
He was commenting on the game when the signal cut out.
entries.contrast: You comment on something. The t is not doubled, because the stress is on KAH-: commented.

entries.meaning: To share information, ideas, or feelings with other people. ---
examples: The two departments barely communicate.
She communicated the bad news gently.
They have been communicating by email for years.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (communicate your ideas clearly), intransitive (they communicate by text)

entries.meaning: To say that you are unhappy or annoyed about something. ---
examples: Guests often complain about the noise.
He complained to the manager.
She has been complaining all week.
entries.contrast: You complain about a problem to a person — never "complain on".

entries.meaning: To tell someone that you admire something about them. ---
examples: People always compliment her on her voice.
He complimented the chef on the sauce.
It felt good to be complimented in front of the whole team.
entries.contrast: compliment (praise) and complement (something that completes) sound alike but differ by one letter, i or e.

entries.meaning: To admit that you have done something wrong or embarrassing. ---
examples: I have to confess I've never read it.
He confessed after six hours of questioning.
She has confessed everything to her lawyer.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (he confessed everything), intransitive (she finally confessed)
entries.contrast: A verb ending in -ss adds -es: confess → confesses.

entries.meaning: Confirm has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Please confirm your appointment by Friday.
The airline confirmed the flight this morning.
The rumor has not been confirmed.
The Senate has to confirm every federal judge.
Lawmakers confirmed her as attorney general.
He was confirmed by a single vote.

senses.head: To say officially that something is true or definite
examples: Please confirm your appointment by Friday.
The airline confirmed the flight this morning.
The rumor has not been confirmed.

senses.head: Of a legislature, to approve someone's appointment to an office
examples: The Senate has to confirm every federal judge.
Lawmakers confirmed her as attorney general.
He was confirmed by a single vote.

entries.русский: подтверждать, подтвердить; утверждать, утвердить (в должности, кандидатуру)

entries.meaning: To tell someone that you are happy about their success or good luck. ---
examples: Let me congratulate you on the new job.
Everyone congratulated her after the show.
He left without congratulating the winner.
entries.contrast: You congratulate someone on something, and the t sounds like ch: kuhn-GRACH-uh-layt.

entries.meaning: Consult has 2 distinct senses.
examples: You should consult a doctor about that cough.
She consulted her notes before answering.
They are consulting with the city about the permit.
She consults for two hospitals in the area.
After he retired, he consulted part-time.
He has been consulting for startups since 2019.

senses.head: To ask a person or a book for information or advice
examples: You should consult a doctor about that cough.
She consulted her notes before answering.
They are consulting with the city about the permit.

senses.head: To work as an outside expert for a company, usually for a fee
examples: She consults for two hospitals in the area.
After he retired, he consulted part-time.
He has been consulting for startups since 2019.

entries.русский: советоваться, посоветоваться; консультироваться; консультировать, работать консультантом
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (consult a lawyer), intransitive (he consults for two firms)

entries.meaning: Contradict has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Don't contradict your grandmother at the table.
His second story contradicted the first.
She has been contradicting herself all morning.
The new figures contradict last year's report.
His second statement contradicted the first.
The two witnesses have contradicted each other on every detail.

senses.head: To say the opposite of what someone else has said
examples: Don't contradict your grandmother at the table.
His second story contradicted the first.
She has been contradicting herself all morning.

senses.head: To be so different from another fact or statement that both cannot be true
examples: The new figures contradict last year's report.
His second statement contradicted the first.
The two witnesses have contradicted each other on every detail.

entries.русский: противоречить; возражать, возразить; противоречить, расходиться с (фактами)

entries.meaning: To make someone believe something or agree to do something. ---
examples: Nothing you say will convince him.
She convinced me to try again.
I am not convinced that it is safe.

entries.meaning: To say what you think is wrong or bad about someone or something. ---
examples: It is easy to criticize from the outside.
The report criticized the hospital's record keeping.
He has been widely criticized for the remark.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (they criticized the plan), intransitive (it is easy to criticize)
entries.contrast: American spelling ends in -ize; British books write criticise.

entries.meaning: Debate has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The two candidates will debate on Tuesday.
Congress debated the bill for three days.
The issue is still being debated.
I debated whether to call her.
He's still debating which offer to take.
Don't debate it too long — the sale ends tonight.

senses.head: To discuss a question formally, with people giving opposite opinions
examples: The two candidates will debate on Tuesday.
Congress debated the bill for three days.
The issue is still being debated.

senses.head: To think something over carefully, weighing two choices
examples: I debated whether to call her.
He's still debating which offer to take.
Don't debate it too long — the sale ends tonight.

entries.русский: обсуждать, обсудить; спорить, дискутировать; раздумывать, колебаться, прикидывать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (they debated the bill), intransitive (the two sides debated for hours)

entries.meaning: To say something clearly, firmly, and often officially. ---
examples: "I'm not going," she declared.
Do you have anything to declare at customs?
The winner has not been declared yet.

entries.meaning: Define has 2 distinct senses.
examples: How would you define "success"?
The contract defined his duties clearly.
The border has never been clearly defined.
One bad season should not define a career.
That summer defined their friendship.
She refuses to be defined by her illness.

senses.head: To say exactly what a word means or what something is
examples: How would you define "success"?
The contract defined his duties clearly.
The border has never been clearly defined.

senses.head: To be the thing that gives someone or something its essential character
examples: One bad season should not define a career.
That summer defined their friendship.
She refuses to be defined by her illness.

entries.русский: определять, определить; давать определение; определять сущность, формировать облик; характеризовать

entries.meaning: Demand has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The workers demand a written answer.
She demanded to see the manager.
They are demanding an apology.
This job demands patience.
The recipe demanded three hours of rising time.
The case has demanded months of work.

senses.head: To ask for something very firmly, as if you have a right to it
examples: The workers demand a written answer.
She demanded to see the manager.
They are demanding an apology.

senses.head: To need something as a necessary condition
examples: This job demands patience.
The recipe demanded three hours of rising time.
The case has demanded months of work.

entries.русский: требовать, потребовать; требовать (о работе, деле), нуждаться в
entries.contrast: demand takes no preposition: "He demanded an explanation," not "demanded for an explanation."

entries.meaning: To say that something is not true. ---
examples: He denies everything.
She denied taking the money.
The company has denied any wrongdoing.
entries.contrast: The y becomes ie: deny → denies → denied.

entries.meaning: To say what someone or something is like. ---
examples: Can you describe the man you saw?
She described the apartment over the phone.
The town has been described as sleepy.
entries.contrast: You describe something to someone: "Describe it to me," never "describe me it."

entries.meaning: To have a different opinion from someone else. ---
examples: I disagree with almost every word of that.
The two doctors disagreed about the treatment.
They have disagreed on this for years.
entries.русский: не соглашаться, не согласиться; расходиться во мнениях
entries.contrast: You disagree with a person and about or on a question.

entries.meaning: To say that something is not true or not fair. ---
examples: Nobody disputes that the road needs work.
She disputed the charge on her bill.
The results are still being disputed.

entries.meaning: To send someone a message by electronic mail. ---
examples: Email me the address when you get a chance.
I emailed her twice last week.
He has been emailing the whole department.
entries.русский: писать по электронной почте, написать письмо (по email)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (email me the file), intransitive (just email when you're ready)

entries.meaning: To give someone the confidence or the advice that makes them want to do something. ---
examples: Teachers should encourage questions.
My uncle encouraged me to apply.
She was encouraged by the early results.
entries.contrast: encourage someone to do something — the to is required.

entries.meaning: To say something suddenly and loudly because of surprise or strong feeling. ---
examples: "You're kidding!" she exclaimed.
Visitors always exclaim over the view.
He kept exclaiming how big the fish was.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive ("You're early!" he exclaimed), intransitive (they exclaimed over the view)

entries.meaning: To make something clear by describing it in detail. ---
examples: Could you explain the rules again?
She explained why the flight was canceled.
He has explained it three times already.
entries.contrast: You explain something to someone: "Explain it to me," never "explain me it."

entries.meaning: To put a thought or a feeling into words. ---
examples: It is hard to express how grateful we are.
She expressed her concerns in a short letter.
Several parents have expressed the same worry.

entries.meaning: To talk about other people's private lives, often unkindly. ---
examples: They gossip about everyone in the building.
We gossiped over coffee for an hour.
She caught them gossiping about her.
entries.contrast: American English keeps one p: gossiped, gossiping — the stress is on GAH-.

entries.meaning: Greet has 2 distinct senses.
examples: He greets every customer by name.
She greeted us at the door.
We were greeted by a very loud dog.
The announcement was greeted with boos.
Fans greeted the trade with relief.
Voters greet every tax hike with anger.

senses.head: To say hello to someone when you meet them
examples: He greets every customer by name.
She greeted us at the door.
We were greeted by a very loud dog.

senses.head: To react to news or to someone's work in a particular way
examples: The announcement was greeted with boos.
Fans greeted the trade with relief.
Voters greet every tax hike with anger.

entries.русский: приветствовать, поприветствовать; здороваться; встречать (реакцией), принимать, воспринять

entries.meaning: To complain in a quiet, unhappy way. ---
examples: The drivers grumble about the new schedule.
He grumbled something and went back to bed.
She has been grumbling since we left.

entries.meaning: To suggest something indirectly instead of saying it openly. ---
examples: She hinted that she might quit.
Stop hinting and just tell me.
He has hinted at a bigger announcement.
entries.contrast: You hint at something: "He hinted at a raise."

entries.meaning: To suggest something without saying it directly. ---
examples: Are you implying that I lied?
Her tone implied that the answer was no.
Nothing in the letter implies a threat.
entries.contrast: The speaker implies; the listener infers. And the y becomes ie: implies, implied.

entries.meaning: Inform has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Please inform the office of any change of address.
They informed us by letter.
We were never informed about the meeting.
Her years as a nurse inform everything she writes.
The decision was informed by two long studies.
Fresh data is informing every choice the team makes.

senses.head: To tell someone about something officially
examples: Please inform the office of any change of address.
They informed us by letter.
We were never informed about the meeting.

senses.head: To shape something and give it its character
examples: Her years as a nurse inform everything she writes.
The decision was informed by two long studies.
Fresh data is informing every choice the team makes.

entries.русский: сообщать, сообщить; информировать; определять, формировать; лежать в основе
entries.contrast: You inform someone of or about something.

entries.meaning: To ask for information, usually politely or formally. ---
examples: I called to inquire about the job.
She inquired whether the room was still free.
Several people have inquired about tickets.
entries.contrast: American English prefers inquire; British writing often spells it enquire.

entries.meaning: To say firmly that something must happen or is true, even when others disagree. ---
examples: He insists that he paid the bill.
She insisted on driving us home.
They kept insisting we stay for dinner.
entries.contrast: You insist on something: "She insisted on paying."

entries.meaning: Instruct has 2 distinct senses.
examples: The judge will instruct the jury this afternoon.
She instructed the class to put their phones away.
We were instructed to wait outside.
She instructs beginners in the pool on Saturday mornings.
A retired pilot instructed our ground school class.
He has been instructing teenagers in woodworking for twenty years.

senses.head: To tell someone officially what they must do
examples: The judge will instruct the jury this afternoon.
She instructed the class to put their phones away.
We were instructed to wait outside.

senses.head: To teach a subject or a skill to someone
examples: She instructs beginners in the pool on Saturday mornings.
A retired pilot instructed our ground school class.
He has been instructing teenagers in woodworking for twenty years.

entries.русский: инструктировать; давать указания; обучать; обучать, обучить; учить, преподавать

entries.meaning: To say something rude that offends someone. ---
examples: I didn't mean to insult anyone.
He insulted the waiter and we left.
She felt insulted by the question.
entries.contrast: The verb is in-SULT; the noun is IN-sult: "He insulted me, and it was a real insult."

entries.meaning: Interrupt has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Please don't interrupt while I'm on the phone.
She interrupted him in the middle of a sentence.
I'm sorry for interrupting.
Rain interrupted the game in the fourth inning.
Nothing is allowed to interrupt the broadcast.
Service has been interrupted twice this week.

senses.head: To start speaking while someone else is still talking
examples: Please don't interrupt while I'm on the phone.
She interrupted him in the middle of a sentence.
I'm sorry for interrupting.

senses.head: To stop something for a while before it is finished
examples: Rain interrupted the game in the fourth inning.
Nothing is allowed to interrupt the broadcast.
Service has been interrupted twice this week.

entries.русский: перебивать, перебить; прерывать, прервать; прерывать, прервать; приостанавливать, приостановить
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (don't interrupt me), intransitive (sorry to interrupt)
entries.contrast: Two r's in the middle: interrupt.

entries.meaning: To ask someone questions, for a job or for a news story. ---
examples: They will interview five candidates on Monday.
A reporter interviewed the neighbors.
I'm being interviewed tomorrow at nine.

entries.meaning: Introduce has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Let me introduce my brother.
She introduced herself to everyone at the table.
We have never been properly introduced.

entries.meaning: Welcome has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Please welcome our next speaker.
They welcomed us like family.
New members are always welcomed at the first meeting.
We welcome any feedback from customers.
Teachers welcomed the change to the schedule.
The ruling has been welcomed by both parties.

senses.head: To greet someone in a friendly way when they arrive
examples: Please welcome our next speaker.
They welcomed us like family.
New members are always welcomed at the first meeting.

senses.head: To be glad that something has happened and to say so
examples: We welcome any feedback from customers.
Teachers welcomed the change to the schedule.
The ruling has been welcomed by both parties.

entries.русский: приветствовать, поприветствовать; радушно встречать; приветствовать (решение), одобрять; охотно принимать

entries.meaning: To speak very quietly, using breath instead of voice. ---
examples: Why are you whispering?
He whispered something to the man beside him.
She whispers whenever she talks about money.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (she whispered a name), intransitive (they whispered in the back)
entries.contrast: The h is silent: whisper is WIS-pur.

entries.meaning: To shout loudly, often in anger or to be heard far away.
examples: Don't yell at your brother.
Somebody yelled from across the street.
The coach was yelling the whole game.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (he yelled my name), intransitive (don't yell)
entries.contrast: yell at someone is angry; yell to someone is just loud.
